content:
I'd like to announce lean-markdown a Lean implementation of both CommonMark and GitHub Flavored Markdown (GFM).

Guarantees

  • Conformant: passes every test in the official CommonMark and cmark-gfm suites.
  • Total: never panics or loops on any input, including adversarial input.
  • Safe: proved to never let an AST leaf's string content produce unescaped HTML markup, or break out of an attribute.
  • Well-formed: for input with no embedded raw HTML, output is proved well-formed HTML.

Both CommonMark and GFM pass raw HTML through verbatim by design. For untrusted input use renderHtmlSafe which guarantees the output is both safe and well formed, including adversarial input.

Hello,

Some feeback :

  • The parsing logic is complex to reason about, if it was using a parser combinator (like prim-parser ) i think you would be able to state proofs more easily and a lot more.
  • I would put the proofs in a dedicated Spec directory, not mixed with the standard unit tests so that it's easy to check what it's proving and what's not.
  • if stronger proofs are a goal, i would formalize the cmark and cmark-gfm spec independently of the implementation. You can see lean-regex project for how it can be done. But this is a lot of work and design.

François G. Dorais said:

Unicode support is at https://github.com/fgdorais/lean4-unicode-basic

Thanks for the pointer. I've just released a new version of the library which uses UnicodeBasic to address most of the Unicode-related known issues. There's still one remaining because UnicodeBasic only supports simple lowercase mapping, but this is still a significant improvement. Many thanks!
I assume the key difference with md4lean is that this has no C dependency and is entirely in Lean?

Eric Wieser said:

I assume the key difference with md4lean is that this has no C dependency and is entirely in Lean?

Exactly, plus the formal safety/well-formedness guarantees.
Please raise an issue on UnicodeBasic requesting full case folding. (That's not exactly the same as lowercase mapping, by the way!)

Is there a reason CommonMark does not recognize all Unicode white space characters?

0009..000D    ; White_Space # Cc   [5] <control-0009>..<control-000D>
0020          ; White_Space # Zs       SPACE
0085          ; White_Space # Cc       <control-0085>
00A0          ; White_Space # Zs       NO-BREAK SPACE
1680          ; White_Space # Zs       OGHAM SPACE MARK
2000..200A    ; White_Space # Zs  [11] EN QUAD..HAIR SPACE
2028          ; White_Space # Zl       LINE SEPARATOR
2029          ; White_Space # Zp       PARAGRAPH SEPARATOR
202F          ; White_Space # Zs       NARROW NO-BREAK SPACE
205F          ; White_Space # Zs       MEDIUM MATHEMATICAL SPACE
3000          ; White_Space # Zs       IDEOGRAPHIC SPACE
It seems to be missing U+000B and U+0085.

François G. Dorais said:

Please raise an issue on UnicodeBasic requesting full case folding. (That's not exactly the same as lowercase mapping, by the way!)

Done: https://github.com/fgdorais/lean4-unicode-basic/issues/155

TIL that case folding and lowercase mapping aren't the same thing. Thanks!

François G. Dorais said:

Is there a reason CommonMark does not recognize all Unicode white space characters?

I'm not a CommonMark expert; I don't know the reasoning behind this. In addition to the codepoints you list, I think it's also missing U+2028 and U+2029? It seems to define whitespace as anything in Zs plus a few additional characters. I don't know why.
